program_overview.title: AI and Machine Learning Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: Twelve months, honestly spent: the mathematics, the models, the modern generative layer, and enough engineering to ship what you train.
program_overview.description:
AI and machine learning is the deepest track we teach, and this masterclass respects that: twelve months from zero, no shortcuts and no skipped mathematics. The foundations phase builds linear algebra, calculus intuition, probability and statistics alongside Python and the data stack, because everything downstream stands on them. Classical machine learning follows with scikit-learn, classification, feature engineering, unsupervised learning, and evaluation taught as the discipline that separates practitioners from demo-makers. The deep learning phase goes through PyTorch, the framework research and industry actually share, into CNNs, computer vision and NLP up to transformers. The final phase is the modern layer: generative AI and LLM engineering, retrieval, fine-tuning concepts, honest evaluation of generated output, plus deployment fundamentals, serving a model, tracking experiments, monitoring drift, and a capstone shipped and defended.

What this course refuses to do is fake the frontier: reinforcement learning, large-scale ML infrastructure and research careers are mapped honestly as next roads, not squeezed into hollow weeks. The reclaimed time goes into depth where it pays: evaluation, error analysis, and the engineering judgment interviews actually probe.

The pace is real: twelve months at two live classes a week plus five to six hours of practice, with two more months in hand when needed. Problem sets after every class, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate, with focused revision and a free retest. Real models, real evaluation, depth over dopamine.
what_makes_this_different: Mathematics first, honestly: linear algebra, calculus and statistics built in-course, not waved at
PyTorch as the spine of deep learning: the framework research and industry actually share
Evaluation and error analysis treated as the core skill, because that is what interviews and real work probe
A genuinely modern generative phase: LLM engineering, retrieval, fine-tuning concepts and honest output evaluation

faqs.question: What does this AI and ML masterclass actually cover?
faqs.answer: The full honest arc: the mathematics (linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics) built alongside Python; classical machine learning with scikit-learn and evaluation as a discipline; deep learning in PyTorch through CNNs, computer vision and NLP to transformers; and the modern layer, LLM engineering with retrieval and fine-tuning judgment, deployment with experiment tracking and monitoring, responsible AI, and a capstone that is trained, evaluated, deployed and defended.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn AI and machine learning properly?
faqs.answer: Twelve months at 2 live classes a week plus 5 to 6 hours of practice, starting from zero, and that is the honest floor when the mathematics is built rather than skipped. The course keeps two more months in hand for learners who need them. Bootcamps compress this by dropping exactly the parts, maths and evaluation, that interviews and real work then expose.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with an exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical modeling task plus written questions from the entire syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest. In this field, honest assessment is the product.

faqs.question: How much mathematics do I need before joining?
faqs.answer: School mathematics. Phase 1 rebuilds linear algebra, calculus intuition, probability and statistics from there, in code and pictures alongside symbols, because every later phase stands on them. Learners who skipped maths for years consistently manage; the course assumes rust, not fluency.

faqs.question: Does the course cover generative AI and LLMs seriously?
faqs.answer: Yes, as engineering rather than magic: how transformers and diffusion actually work, prompting with evaluation harnesses, retrieval-augmented generation over real documents, fine-tuning judgment (what it changes, costs, and when it is wrong), structured output and function calling, and the cost-latency-quality triangle. The month ends with a retrieval assistant you built and scored honestly.

faqs.question: Will I be able to deploy models, or just train them in notebooks?
faqs.answer: Deploy. The final phase covers serving a model behind an API, experiment tracking, monitoring and drift, and the capstone is required to ship that way with a model card. Full-scale ML infrastructure is its own profession and is mapped honestly as a next road; what you leave with is the working end of it.

faqs.question: Do I need an expensive GPU machine?
faqs.answer: No. A normal laptop is enough: heavy training runs on free cloud notebooks with GPU time, and the toolchain, Python, scikit-learn, PyTorch, tracking tools, is free throughout. Where a hosted LLM API is used, free tiers cover the coursework.

faqs.question: What are the fees?
faqs.answer: Group classes are ₹1,499 per month, with 2 live classes a week in batches capped at 10 learners. A mini batch of 3-4 learners is ₹2,999 per month, and personal 1-on-1 classes are ₹4,999 per month. International learners pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Can I try a class before enrolling?
faqs.answer: Yes, a free demo class with no commitment: book at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact or message us on WhatsApp at +91 91233 66161. You will train a small model inside the demo itself.

faqs.question: Are classes live or recorded?
faqs.answer: Live, always: small groups with a real instructor reading your actual notebooks, never pre-recorded videos. ML fails silently, leaked data, misread metrics, and live eyes on your work is the only honest way to catch it early.
